title: fix(tooling): make check:type-source-resolution per-program, not per-package
body:
Fixes #11490

`scripts/check-type-source-resolution.mjs` built every package's tsc program from `join(pkg.dir, 'tsconfig.json')` and nothing else, so every other tsc program in the package sat outside its declared population. That is not an exotic case here: the repair this repo **prescribes** for a hidden test layer — stated in AGENTS.md and in `check-type-check-coverage.mjs`'s TESTS_COVERED docs — is precisely a **sibling** `tsconfig.test.json` named in the `typecheck` script, and CI runs it on every PR. Following the house pattern was therefore what made an exposure invisible.

The population is now **every `tsconfig*.json` a package's `typecheck` script NAMES**.

## The card's own measurement, re-derived on current `main` before the change

Both legs on `59972075e`, on `packages/triggers/trigger-record-change` — 7 test files carrying the same four dist-resolved type imports:

| the same files, put through | pre-change gate |
| --- | --- |
| the **build** config (drop `"**/*.test.ts"` from its `exclude`) | exit **1** — `✗ @objectstack/trigger-record-change: NEW dist-resolved type import(s) since this entry was measured: @objectstack/driver-sql, @objectstack/formula, @objectstack/objectql, @objectstack/service-automation.` |
| the prescribed **sibling** config (the tree as it stands) | exit **0** — `check-type-source-resolution OK — 77 packages with a tsconfig.json scanned; 51 registered` |

The asymmetry had not closed. The mutation was proven on disk in both directions (exclusion-anchor occurrence count 1 → 0 → restored, `git diff --stat` non-empty, `git status` clean afterwards) and restored under `trap restore EXIT INT TERM`.

## The acceptance test, two-sided

After the change the sibling-config spelling reports **identically** to the build-config spelling. Both sides are pinned as self-test fixtures rather than left to a one-off run:

* **(17) `packages/sibling-config`** — build config excludes the test layer, sibling `tsconfig.test.json` named by `typecheck`, exposure reachable only through the sibling. Must be reported.
* **(18) `packages/build-config-twin`** — byte-identical files and import, reached through the build config. Must be reported.
* the assertion is not "both are reported" but that `measured.get('@fx/sibling-config')` **equals** `measured.get('@fx/build-config-twin')`, and that both equal exactly `['@fx/spec']`.
* **(19) `packages/decorative-config`** — identical to (17) except that **no script names the sibling**. Must **not** be reported.

## Non-vacuity: an ablation on the real tree, both gates on one mutated tree

A dist-resolved import (`@objectstack/metadata-core`) planted in `packages/triggers/trigger-record-change/src/record-change-trigger.test.ts` — a file the build config excludes and the sibling includes:

```
PRE-CHANGE gate on the MUTATED tree
  PRE_EXIT=0
  check-type-source-resolution OK — 77 packages with a tsconfig.json scanned; 51 registered ...

WIDENED gate on the SAME MUTATED tree
  POST_EXIT=1
  check-type-source-resolution FAILED
  ✗ @objectstack/trigger-record-change: NEW dist-resolved type import(s) since this entry
    was measured: @objectstack/metadata-core (via tsconfig.test.json).
```

Mutation proven on disk both directions (marker count 0 → 1 → 0, `git status --porcelain` empty after restore), restored under a `trap`, and both gates re-run green on the restored tree.

## Why NAMED, not every `tsconfig*.json` on disk

The criterion is "the `typecheck` script names it", never "the glob matches it". A config no script invokes is decorative: putting it in the population reports imports no tsc program ever resolves, and a gate that looks stronger while measuring something nobody runs is **worse** than the state it replaced, because it *reads* as covered.

Measured across the workspace at the widening: **16 configs across 15 packages** join the population, and `packages/cli/tsconfig.build.json` — present on disk, named by no script — correctly stays out. 0 package manifests in this workspace reference a tsconfig with a directory prefix, so the basename property of the predicate (documented in the new module's header) has no instance today; names are resolved against the package's own directory regardless.

## The registry re-baseline, with its numbers

⚠️ This is a **population widening = gate strengthening**. Nothing about the repo changed and no new exposure was admitted — the same imports were always there, in tsc programs CI has been running on every PR, and the instrument could not see them. Both figures from `--list` on the same checkout:

| | programs | packages | registry entries | package-dep pairs | clean |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **before** | 77 | 77 | 51 | 221 | 26 |
| **after** | 93 | 77 | 54 | 233 | 23 |

so **+16 programs, +3 entries, +12 pairs**. What the widening turned up, all of it previously invisible:

* **3 new entries**, each reached only through `tsconfig.scripts.json`: `@objectstack/plugin-webhooks`, `@objectstack/service-messaging`, `@objectstack/service-realtime` — all `['@objectstack/spec']`.
* `@objectstack/client` **+4** via `tsconfig.test.json`: `driver-sqlite-wasm`, `objectql`, `plugin-hono-server`, `runtime`.
* `@objectstack/trigger-record-change` **+4** via `tsconfig.test.json`: `driver-sql`, `formula`, `objectql`, `service-automation` — the card's own four.
* `@objectstack/plugin-auth` **+1** via `tsconfig.examples.json`: `plugin-hono-server`.

Nothing was baselined away and no gate was weakened. The registry's docblock now carries the before/after and an explicit refusal: the precedent is available only when the SET OF PROGRAMS changed, which is a change to the gate file, never to a package.

## The shared predicate

`configsNamedByTypecheck` was local to `check-type-check-coverage.mjs`. It is now `scripts/typecheck-configs.mjs`, imported by both gates — a second copy of that regex is how the two answers drift, and the symptom of drift is a green gate on either side. Its cases moved with it and **both** gates fold them in.

The extraction is provably behaviour-preserving, not merely believed to be:

* both extracted function bodies are **byte-identical** to the originals (`diff` of the `awk`-extracted spans against `59972075e`: 6 lines and 13 lines, no output);
* `check-type-check-coverage.mjs`'s structural pass prints **byte-identical output** at `59972075e` and at this branch's HEAD on the same tree.

## Diagnostics

A widened diagnostic that only names the package is one an author cannot act on — they open `tsconfig.json`, find no such import, and conclude the gate is wrong. Every finding now names the program: `@objectstack/spec (via tsconfig.scripts.json)`, and config-level defects (unreadable configs, `@pkg*` star traps, dead `paths` targets) are reported as `packages/x/tsconfig.test.json: ...` rather than against the package.

## Census guard

The widening can go quiet — `configsNamedByTypecheck` returning an empty set for every package reverts this gate to exactly its old per-package behaviour, every remaining program still scans, and the summary reads like a clean repo. A new census leg fails when **no** package runs more than one tsc program, and it carries its own positive control: a purpose-built single-program tree is asserted to trip it, and the real fixture tree is asserted **not** to.

## Verification

All at HEAD `e3abf9a1d`. Gate families derived live with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (never a hand-written list); each verdict is the gate's own printed line, exit codes captured before any pipe.

| gate | exit | its own verdict line |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `check:type-source-resolution` | 0 | `check-type-source-resolution --self-test OK` / `OK — 93 tsc program(s) across 77 packages scanned ...; 54 registered` |
| `check:type-check-coverage` | 0 | `OK — 65/78 workspace packages type-checked (plus the root), 13 in the DEBT ledger ..., 1 exempt` |
| `check:entry-guard` | 0 | `155 scripts/ file(s) — every entry guard goes through invoked-as.mjs` |
| `check:parse-guard` | 0 | `154 scripts/ file(s) — every TypeScript parse goes through ts-parse.mjs` |
| `check:agent-test-spelling` | 0 | `0 violations — 365 file(s) ...` |
| `check:pnpm-filter-targets` | 0 | `135/168 --filter occurrence(s) across 26 file(s) resolve against 78 workspace package(s)` |
| `check:cross-package-test-inputs` | 0 | `OK: 16 package(s) read outside themselves, all declared` |
| `check-ci-filter-parity.mjs` | 0 | `OK: all 96 declared cross-package glob(s) (81 unique) are covered ...` |
| `check-cross-package-test-inputs.mjs` | 0 | `OK: 16 package(s) read outside themselves, all declared` |
| `check:nul-bytes` | 0 | `OK (scanned 6639 text file(s) ...; no raw ASCII control bytes)` |
| `typecheck-configs.mjs --self-test` | 0 | `typecheck-configs --self-test OK -- 11 cases hold.` |

**Declared narrowing, one item.** `check:type-check-debt` is `--self-test && --re-measure`. Its `--self-test` leg is the same one run green above under `check:type-check-coverage`. Its `--re-measure` leg refused to run and measured nothing — `Error: --re-measure cannot run: 56 workspace dependenc(ies) of the ledgered packages have no built type entry point on disk` — it needs a full `turbo run build` of the workspace first, which is CI's run (`lint.yml` builds the closure before this step). Left to CI, and named here rather than passed over. The by-construction argument that it cannot move: the predicate bodies are byte-identical and the structural pass output is byte-identical.

**Lint, narrowed, and the narrowing measured.** `eslint --no-inline-config` over the 3 changed files: 3 files, **0 errors, 0 warnings** (counts read from `--format json`, not from a summary line). Three pieces of evidence that this is a measurement rather than a silence: (1) the population is read from eslint's own config — `ESLint#isPathIgnored` is `false` for all three and `calculateConfigForFile` reports the 2 rules that govern `scripts/*.mjs`; (2) the file count comes from the JSON payload; (3) `eslint.config.mjs` never enables type-aware linting for any file (its own header states and measures this), so no untouched file's verdict can move on account of this diff. Positive control: a planted `comment-swallow/no-code-inside-block-comment` violation in the new module drove the same command to exit 1 naming that rule, `node --check` confirmed the mutant still parsed (an assertion-red, not a crash-red), and the restored file returned to exit 0.

## No changeset

Dev tooling only — three files under `scripts/`, nothing published and nothing user-visible. `skip-changeset` applied.
